assembly_notes: Heavy-duty desk paper punch. One grounded `base` part carries the sole, rubber feet, the deck and one annular die per station; the deck is a CadQuery solid whose chip passages and drawer cavity are cut per station and per chip candidate. A `frame` part is FIXED on the rear of the deck and always exposes the same two interfaces: a head beam bored once per station (plus a plunger bore when the plunger is active) and a pivot line at (pivot_x, pivot_z). punch_station_count carriages ride PRISMATIC straight down from that beam, each guide stem running in its bore with a 0.8 mm fit over the whole stroke and each pin entering its own die ring and deck passage at full stroke, so nothing is retained by an overlap allowance. frame_form varies the structure around those interfaces (one-piece cast hood, built-up twin side plates, or a one-piece deep-throat C profile). actuation varies the input: a single long ball-grip lever or a twin-strap U-grip lever on the pivot line, a drag-link lever whose link mimics the handle and runs outboard of the head beam, or a press plunger whose PRISMATIC stem mimics carriage 0 so the driver plate can never be pressed into a carriage that has not moved. paper_guide varies registration (a graduated side rail with two sliding stops, or bed lateral and depth fences) and rides on the deck top plus the fixed bed thickness when that chip candidate is active. chip_handling is either a pull-out drawer in the deck cavity or a fixed bed plate. base_length_m, throat_depth_m and lever_reach_m are honest continuous parameters that derive the punch line, head overhang, frame profile, handle length, guide travel and drawer travel; palette and rail graduations are non-core.
